topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into cancer-causing viruses established that transformation can originate in altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental tests of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how laboratory assays establish whether a gene or mutation produces transformed cellular properties.

topics.label: Functional classification and effects of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects and show why those effects depend on the affected pathway and the particular mutation.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defects in genome maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures to preserve genome fidelity produce sequence or chromosomal instability and its cellular consequences.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing and order of mutation acquisition influence progression from normal colorectal epithelium to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Inherited cancer predisposition and tumor suppressor defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited tumor suppressor defects predispose cells to cancer without necessarily remaining essential to established malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture close, further reading and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the learning outcomes and offers questions, recommended reading and a preview of the next lecture.
